changes_made.explanation: Consolidated duplicate task entries, normalized model names to standard forms, and simplified output descriptions while maintaining accuracy. Removed 'car reviews' as a dataset since it's the output type, not an input dataset.
No automatic metrics were used to evaluate NLG outputs in this paper. The regression models (MSE, R2) were used for predictive modeling, not for evaluating generated text quality.
No LLMs were used as judges/evaluators of generated outputs. ChatGPT was mentioned as an example of generation capabilities but not for evaluation purposes.

guideline: Participants estimated lower and upper thresholds for numerical features (acceleration, mileage, maximum speed, power output, displacement) that would make evaluative expressions acceptable in car review sentences

changes_made.explanation: Changed answer from No to Yes because the paper clearly conducted human evaluations to validate their regression models. Improved guideline description and consolidated criteria to be more general rather than listing each feature separately.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on validating regression models for predicting when to use evaluative language in data-to-text generation, rather than evaluating the quality of generated text itself. The human evaluation was conducted to validate the regression thresholds, not to rate generated outputs. The extraction was generally accurate but missed that human evaluation was conducted.
